chunk_map.heading: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 line 7: 'Before editing files or cutting rules, decide whether the re-send is done enough, should be stopped, or counts as the partial artefact.' -- 'the re-send', 'the partial artefact' read as un-introduced on a cold read of this file alone, but the enclosing module file (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md, '## Start here', which renders immediately before this exercise link in both deck and long-read) already states 'decide whether to wait, stop M5, or accept the partial session as the artefact' -- per rule 1's module-include-order carve-out ('vocabulary the enclosing module file's signposting introduced counts as prior context'), this resolves. Second candidate: chunk 2 line 29 'the quote rule re-asserted' -- not named verbatim anywhere, but chunk 1's prompt (line 24 expansion) ends 'For every claim, quote a specific moment from the artefacts. Don't generalise' one slide back, the only plausible antecedent a sequential reader holds -- passes as immediate continuation (rule 1's own NOT-violation carve-out), not a second/ambiguous candidate. Remaining nouns (task.md, plan.md, the 'Run coordinates' block, ./CLAUDE.local.md) are session artifacts the student's own M4/M5 sessions produced -- exempt under the session-artifacts-in-exercises carve-out.

rules_evaluated.na_reason: no markdown links in body (grep for '](' returns nothing); the M4/M5 references name their source directly (M5 worktree, m4/<slug> branch, task.md, plan.md), never by file position, so the shape this rule targets does not occur.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE 'the [a-zA-Z-]+ you (did|saw|caught|found|wrote|built|made|just [a-z]+)' on the body projection: no output. The only backward-pointing beats named are M4 and M5 (chunk 0: 'the un-packaged Module 4 send-off' is in the module file, not this exercise file -- but within this file itself: 'M5 worktree', 'M5's session', 'the m4/<slug> branch', 'the m5/<slug> branch'), both confirmed present and ordered immediately before this file's own module in site/layouts/curriculum.js's TRAININGS['agentic-engineering-101'].modules array (run-the-first-experiment, learn-from-the-test, spot-gaps-build-the-loop, in that order). No dead-beat shape found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body; this is a diff-and-cut exercise, not a live-demo beat.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunks 1-4 each carry a self-contained instruction plus either a prompt card or an explicit decision rule (chunk 4: 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged... One rule cut, no more.'). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (chunk 1) both diffs and asks to rank via the prompt's closing line 'which gap matters most? Rank by damage-to-a-future-session'; 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (chunk 2) matches its three push-back bullets; 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (chunk 3) matches the cut-prompt; 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (chunk 4) matches the approve/push-back bullets. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

grep -noE 'Not [A-Za-z][^.]*\. Not [A-Za-z][^.]*\.' on the body: no output. Checked remaining sub-items by read: no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (closest is chunk 0 line 13 'two sessions are enough to place every lesson' -- a substantive teaching claim about the method, not a claim the exercise itself is valuable/impressive, and is separately carried by the maintainer block's accept-note against check_writing §21's world-claim test); no number-with-retraction (only number in body is the 'Time: 20 minutes' label); no abstraction-noun stack (vocabulary is concrete throughout: branch, worktree, transcript, rules file); no empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|Connections)\b' on the body projection -> no matches. Vocabulary throughout (branch, worktree, transcript, diff, rules file, verifier, plan) is ordinary engineer register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest-to-violating case: chunk 0 (title slide, lines 3-13) carries five bolded labels -- **Time:**, **Session**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:** -- over a naive count of the <=1-bold-per-slide budget. Each is a <=2-word label (widget/label chrome), not a bolded lead sentence, and the same shape ('**Time:**' opening the title slide) recurs across the exercise-file template corpuswide, so the count is the template's doing, not this file's -- the rule's own instruction to check whether the module/file template mandates the bold before charging §9. The file's own maintainer block (line 59, 'Emphasis pass 2026-07-09') independently attests this exact shape: 'bullet leads plain; bold only on widget / label chrome, per theory-plan.md ... + check_slides.md §9.' Chunks 1-4 carry zero bold markup (grep '\*\*' confirms all five hits sit in lines 3-13).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: signals.slide_count: 4 matches a manual count of '##' headings in the raw body (4), confirming nothing silently dropped. The body has no top-level prose outside a '##' chunk or the pre-first-heading title slide. This file is included via a standalone-paragraph link from the module file and renders under the module's own '.phase--exercise' wrapper by the mechanism every AE101 exercise uses -- not something this file's own content could opt out of. git diff 4589f1d5..HEAD on this file touches only bullet/maintainer prose, no tier marker, phase marker, or heading, so deck presence is unaffected by this revision.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four body headings are imperative exercise-shape constructions, none declarative: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (L17), 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (L26), 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (L32), 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (L41). The exercise stays diagnostic/procedural throughout and never reaches a stated law that would call for a declarative heading, so the claim-heading requirement for law/consolidation slides does not apply here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest-to-violating case: chunk 3 line 35 'Rules-files have a half-life. Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.' -- reads general but it is the only statement of this framing anywhere in the file (not doctrine restatement, class a), it is about rules-files, not the training's own pedagogy (not class b), and it does not close the chunk -- the prompt card follows it (not an aphorism kicker, class c). It supplies the rationale for the cut the next line asks for. No instance of any of the three classes found elsewhere in the file.
